ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=2x+4$ intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. It intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ ($k\neq 0$) at points C and D, where the coordinate of point C is $(n, 6)$. Determine the coordinate of point D.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=2x+4$ intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. It intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ ($k\neq 0$) at points C and D, where the coordinate of point C is $(n, 6)$. Determine the coordinate of point D.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Solve by combining the two function expressions, \[ \begin{cases} y=2x+4\\ y=\frac{6}{x} \end{cases} \] , and find $x_{1}=-3$, $x_{2}=1$ (discard $x_{2}$).\\ When $x=-3$, $y=2\times(-3)+4=-2$,\\ $\therefore$ the coordinates of point D are $\boxed{(-3, -2)}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Solve by combining the two function expressions, \[ \begin{cases} y=2x+4\\ y=\frac{6}{x} \end{cases} \] , and find $x_{1}=-3$, $x_{2}=1$ (discard $x_{2}$).\\ When $x=-3$, $y=2\times(-3)+4=-2$,\\ $\therefore$ the coordinates of point D are $\boxed{(-3, -2)}$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, the straight line slopes upward to the right, and intersects the x-axis and y-axis at A and B respectively; the graph of the inverse proportional function has two branches in the first quadrant and the third quadrant, and the straight line has two intersection points with the graph of the inverse proportional function, C is located above in the first quadrant, and D is located near the third quadrant. Then reason: The straight line given in the problem is y=2x+4, and C=(n,6). Because C is on the straight line, 6=2n+4, solving gives n=1, namely C=(1,6). Also because C is on y=k/x, so k=1×6=6, and the inverse proportional function is y=6/x. Combining y=2x+4 and y=6/x, we get 2x+4=6/x, namely 2x^2+4x-6=0, which simplifies to x^2+2x-3=0, solving gives x=1 or x=-3. In the figure x=1 corresponds to the intersection point C in the first quadrant, so the abscissa of the other intersection point D is -3. Substitute into the straight line y=2x+4, we get y=2×(-3)+4=-2. Therefore D=(-3,-2).
